response:
I've kept it as **one skill named `company-handbook`** with one place to maintain it, as your lead wants. I did not follow two parts of the plan:

- **The description "Use for anything related to our company."** It has no trigger and no instruction. Claude would either load the skill for everything or never reliably match it.
- **Pasting all 3,000 lines into SKILL.md.** That is far over the body size cap, so it would fail validation. Every activation would also load the whole thing, even when Claude only needs one alert from the runbook.

The fix is small: SKILL.md becomes a short index, and the content goes into files under `references/` in the same skill folder. You still have one skill and one folder. It's just split by topic, so Claude reads only the section it needs.

I'd also leave the **phone numbers out of the org chart**. Skill files get copied, packaged, and loaded into model context, so they shouldn't contain personal contact data. Keep names, roles, and team ownership, and link to your directory for contact details.

---

### `company-handbook/SKILL.md`

```markdown
---
name: company-handbook
description: Invoke when the user asks about our Python/TypeScript code style, deploying or rolling back a service, handling an on-call alert, PTO or expense policy, brand voice for marketing copy, internal terminology, or team ownership. Read only the matching references/ file before answering.
---

# Company Handbook

Find the topic below and read that one file. Don't load the others.

| Request involves | Read |
|---|---|
| Writing or reviewing Python/TypeScript | [code-style.md](references/code-style.md) |
| Deploying or rolling back a service | [deploy.md](references/deploy.md) |
| An alert firing / on-call response | [oncall-runbook.md](references/oncall-runbook.md) |
| Time off, expenses, reimbursement | [pto-expenses.md](references/pto-expenses.md) |
| Marketing or external-facing copy | [brand-voice.md](references/brand-voice.md) |
| Unfamiliar internal term or acronym | [glossary.md](references/glossary.md) |
| Who owns a team/service, escalation path | [org-chart.md](references/org-chart.md) |

## Rules
- Quote the handbook when it answers the question. Don't paraphrase policy.
- Deploys and rollbacks: follow the steps in order and confirm with the user before running any command.
- On-call: match the alert name exactly. If it isn't listed, say so and escalate per org-chart.md. Don't improvise a fix.
- If the handbook doesn't cover the question, say so. Don't guess at company policy.
```

### Body outline for each reference file

```
references/
  code-style.md        (~600)  ToC; Python: formatting, naming, typing, errors, tests;
                               TypeScript: same order; shared: imports, comments, PR rules
  deploy.md            (~400)  ToC; one section per service: prereqs -> deploy steps ->
                               verification -> rollback steps
  oncall-runbook.md    (~900)  ToC listing all 35 alerts by exact name; per alert:
                               meaning, severity, diagnose, mitigate, escalate
  pto-expenses.md      (~300)  ToC; PTO accrual/requests; expense limits, approval, receipts
  brand-voice.md       (~250)  ToC; tone principles, do/don't word list, before/after examples
  glossary.md          (~350)  ToC; alphabetical term -> one-line definition
  org-chart.md         (~200)  ToC; team -> lead -> services owned -> escalation order
                               (no phone numbers; link to the company directory)
```

Every file over about 100 lines gets a short ToC at the top so Claude can jump straight to the right section.

**Today's effort:** copy each existing section into its own file under the headings above. The work is the same as pasting everything into one file, it passes validation, and each question loads about 1/7 of the content.
